newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish PM stands by wealth tax for A list shares.
newsitem.headline: Swedish PM stands by wealth tax for A list shares.

text.p: Sweden's Prime Minister Goran Persson said on Thursday the government would not cut a wealth tax for main owners of companies listed on the Stockholm Stock Exchange's main A list.

"We don't want a Sweden where food prices rise because wealth taxes are removed," Persson told parliament during a debate. "We don't want a Sweden that undermines health care and schools to get lower share taxes."

A 1996 law forces Swedes with wealth exceeding 900,000 crowns to pay 1.5 percent tax on 100 percent of the value of shares listed on the A list, up from 75 percent, while shares on the smaller O list remain exempt from tax.

The law has prompted companies such as fashion retailer Hennes & Mauritz, media group Marieberg AB, construction group Lundbergs and investment company Latour to flee from the A to the O list this month.

The recent share transfers were triggered by a law adopted by parliament in June reaffirming that main shareholders -- people holding more than 25 percent of votes -- have to pay tax for shares listed on the A list before 1991.
Companies that started trading on the A list before 1991 had hoped parliament would change the 1996 law.
